body:
## Pull request overview

This PR addresses blank report content in the console by adding runtime data loading to `ReportView` and wiring the loaded `data`/`loading` props into the `ReportViewer` schema so report sections can render against fetched records.

**Changes:**
- Add runtime data state + `useEffect` fetching logic in `ReportView` (inline data, `dataSource` config, or `objectName`).
- Pass `data` and `loading` into the `ReportViewer` schema.
- Add integration tests for ReportView data loading scenarios.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 9 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| apps/console/src/components/ReportView.tsx | Adds runtime data loading and passes `data`/`loading` to the report viewer schema. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/ReportView.test.tsx | Adds ReportView integration tests around metadata + data loading behavior. |

The “display loading state while fetching data” test doesn’t assert that any loading UI is shown. Right now it only waits for `/loading/i` to disappear, which can also inadvertently wait for the report data fetch to finish. Consider explicitly asserting the presence of the ReportViewer loading message (e.g., “Loading report data...”) before resolving the delayed promise, then asserting it disappears.

The objectName integration test doesn’t actually verify that runtime data was fetched/passed to `ReportViewer` (it only checks for toolbar/print button text). This could still pass even if `dataSource.find` is never called or `data` is empty. Consider spying on `dataSource.find` (or rendering assertions against expected rows/aggregations) to ensure the core bugfix (wiring `data` into the viewer schema) is covered.

The early return `if (!reportData || !dataSource)` prevents using inline `reportData.data` when no `dataSource` prop is provided, and it can also leave `dataLoading` stuck `true` if the previous report was fetching and the next `reportData` switches to inline/no-source. Consider checking `reportData.data` before gating on `dataSource`, and explicitly resetting `dataLoading` to `false` in these early-return branches.

This effect starts async fetches without any cancellation/sequence guard. If `reportData` changes quickly or the component unmounts, a slower request can still call `setReportRuntimeData`/`setDataLoading` and overwrite newer state. The repo uses a `cancelled` flag pattern in similar effects (e.g., AdapterProvider/MetadataProvider); consider adopting the same pattern here (or an AbortController if the adapter supports it).

`$filter` is being set to `reportData.filters`, but `ReportSchema.filters` is an array of `ReportFilter` objects, while `QueryParams.$filter` is documented as a record/expression object. Passing the array through will either be ignored or misinterpreted by adapters. Consider translating `ReportFilter[]` into the adapter’s expected filter shape (or omitting `$filter` until that translation exists).
```suggestion

```

The test adapter is constructed with `baseUrl: ''`, but the MSW handlers in `apps/console/src/mocks/server.ts` are set up for `http://localhost:3000/...` and other integration tests use `http://localhost:3000` for both client and data source. Using an empty baseUrl may cause requests to miss the handlers or fail URL construction in Node. Consider aligning this with the other MSW integration tests (e.g., `baseUrl: 'http://localhost:3000'`).
```suggestion
      baseUrl: 'http://localhost:3000',
```

The “inline data” test currently has no assertions and will pass regardless of behavior. It should either be completed (e.g., ensure `find` is not called and that some inline row content is rendered) or removed to avoid giving a false sense of coverage.

When starting a new fetch for a different `reportData`, `reportRuntimeData` is not cleared until the request completes, so the UI can briefly render stale data from the previous report under the new report definition. Consider clearing `reportRuntimeData` (or tracking which report the data belongs to) when setting `dataLoading(true)`.
